observable_outcome: A Requirement in needs-input carries its question through the running system: an application command records the question, its reason class, its options with each option's impact, and what stops and what continues while it waits; a second command lets an authenticated owner answer it, resuming the same Requirement and creating no new one; GET /v1/requirements/{requirement_id} returns the question as an optional detail field that is absent (never synthesised) when no question was recorded; both commands are reachable over HTTP; and while the Requirement waits, no new claim is issued and no held claim is extended for its Increments, with the displayed stop scope asserted against that enforcement. internal/domain is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Measure before designing anything into code, and record each measurement in the evidence. (i) No application code calls domain.DecideRequirement today; confirm by grep and report the hit count. (ii) domain.RequirementNeedInput is allowed only from framing, active and evaluating, and domain.RequirementReadyCommand is allowed from framing, waiting and needs-input (internal/domain/model.go around lines 453 and 468); quote both. (iii) No domain transition revokes or releases an active lease early: ExpireLease refuses when at is before ExpiresAt, RotateLease only revokes as a side effect of issuing a successor, and LeaseReleased/LeaseRevoked are not produced by any exported transition from the outside. If any of these measurements disagrees with what is written here, stop and escalate to the tech_lead instead of adjusting the design or the numbers.

A2. The side table, not the aggregate. Add a port RequirementNeedsInputRepository to internal/application/ports.go and to UnitOfWork, with a save and a read keyed by Requirement id, carrying an application-level record type (name it HumanInputRequest) that holds: question, reason_class, reason, options (each with option_id, summary, impact), stopped_scope, continuing_scope, asked_at, asked_by, and the answer fields answered_at, answered_option_id, answered_by. Nothing is added to domain.Requirement and internal/domain is not edited. Follow the ControlRequestedByRepository comment and implementation idiom in ports.go, internal/store/memory/store.go (around line 451) and internal/store/firestore/store.go (around line 1042) exactly, including the write-once-per-key behaviour, with the single documented difference that the answer fields are written by a second, later transaction on the same row and must never erase the recorded question.

A3. Command 1, the ask. Add Service.RequestHumanInput to internal/application: caller roles runner and scheduler only (owner must be refused); idempotent by request_id through the existing s.mutate plus u.Idempotency path with a request fingerprint, exactly as Capture does; transitions the Requirement with domain.RequirementCommand{Kind: domain.RequirementNeedInput} against a caller-supplied expected Requirement version; writes the question row in the same transaction; records an event through s.record; and stages no outbox item. Evaluate no domain.Permit (precedent: Plan at service.go:670 and Prepare at service.go:762 mutate canonical state with no Permit), and assert in a test that no outbox item is staged.

A4. Command 2, the answer. Add Service.AnswerHumanInput: caller role owner only (runner and scheduler must be refused); idempotent by request_id in the same way; requires an option_id present in the recorded option set and the Requirement's expected version; transitions the same Requirement with domain.RequirementCommand{Kind: domain.RequirementReadyCommand}; records answered_at, answered_option_id and answered_by (the domain.RequestedBy of the authenticated owner) on the existing row without erasing the question; and evaluates domain.Permit with Kind domain.PermitIntake against the installation target, exactly as Capture does at service.go:635. There is no default option, no expiry-based selection and no timeout that answers anything.

A5. Nothing new is created and nothing is lost. Assert in a test that after a successful answer the Requirement id is identical, the total number of Requirements is unchanged, and the status is ready; and that a second answer to the same (already answered) question is refused by the domain transition itself, not by an application flag. Assert that every rejection path -- non-owner caller, unknown option_id, stale expected version, already answered -- leaves the Requirement status, the Requirement version and the stored question row unchanged.

A6. The claim guarantee, closed on the issuing side. Make Service.Claim refuse when the parent Requirement of the requested Increment is in needs-input (resolve it via domain.Increment.RequirementID), and make Service.Renew refuse when the lease's Increment has a parent Requirement in needs-input. Assert both refusals, and assert that a lease held at the moment of the ask is not extended by a later Renew. State plainly in the evidence what is and is not guaranteed: no new claim is issued and no held claim is extended, and a lease already held lapses at its existing ExpiresAt because no domain transition can revoke it early. Do not write a claim stronger than that.

A7. The displayed stop scope agrees with the enforcement. Define stopped_scope and continuing_scope over a closed vocabulary and assert its closure (an out-of-vocabulary value is rejected), following the TestRequestedByActorTypeIsAClosedEnum idiom. Then assert agreement: the vocabulary entry meaning 'new claims for this Requirement are stopped' is reported for a needs-input Requirement if and only if Claim actually refuses for one of its Increments in the same test run. reason_class is closed to exactly {destructive-irreversible, limit-change, ambiguous-requirement}, derived from the capability declaration's user_action, and an option with an empty impact is rejected.

A8. The read view, following V2-052. Add the optional field to RequirementDetailView as a pointer with omitempty, populated from the side table and returned as a copy so callers cannot mutate the stored value through the pointer, exactly as requestedByView does in internal/application/readmodels.go. Assert that a Requirement with no row reads with the field absent, including a Requirement whose status is needs-input but which has no row: the field stays absent and no question is synthesised from the status. Add a test in the shape of TestLegacyRequirementWithoutRequestedByStillReads and name it so the precedent is visible. RequirementView (the list page) and Export are not changed.

A9. HTTP. Add POST /v1/requirements/{requirement_id}:request-input (runner or scheduler role) and POST /v1/requirements/{requirement_id}:answer-input (owner role) to internal/api/api.go in the POST switch's default branch, following the prefix-plus-suffix idiom already used for /v1/leases/{lease_id}:renew and /v1/executions/{execution_id}:start, and make sure the new prefixes cannot be swallowed by the existing GET /v1/requirements/ prefix branch. Declare both paths and their request/response schemas in contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml with additionalProperties false and explicit required lists, add the needs-input object to RequirementDetailResponse, and use no field name containing password, credential, raw_prompt or raw_provider_output. Assert the role gates over HTTP (401 unauthenticated, 403 wrong role) in internal/api/api_test.go.

A10. Bounded sizes. Every free-text field is length-bounded and the option list is count-bounded, with the bounds asserted and the rejection of an over-long value asserted. Reuse the existing MaxPageSize-style constant idiom rather than inlining magic numbers, and state the chosen bounds in the evidence.

A11. Owner console, additive only. Add a needs-input block to internal/web/owner.html and internal/web/owner.js that renders the question, the reason, each option with its impact, and both scope lists, and submits a selected option only on an explicit owner action. internal/web is edited by V2-066 in parallel: your edit must be strictly additive, must not rewrite or remove the sibling task's section, and if a merge conflict appears in these two files you stop and escalate rather than reverting the sibling's work.

A12. Documentation, without a fixed point. Add prose to the cap-human-input-request section of docs/preview/capabilities.md describing what the owner can now see and how to answer. Add no new <a id=...> anchor (the capability anchor bijection asserted by TestCapabilityAnchorBijectionBothDirections and by TestFoundationReleaseContractBaseline must be preserved), touch no other capability section, and write no digest value into any document. docs/preview/index.md and docs/stable/index.md and their release markers are not touched.

A13. Do not overclaim. Record explicitly in the evidence that this task wires the surface only: the automatic decision to ask (the failure-model routes in docs/architecture/failure-model.md that send policy-denied, budget-exceeded and unclassifiable failures to needs-input) is not implemented here, and cap-human-input-request is therefore not exercised by this task. Do not write 'capability exercised' or 'preview journey passed' anywhere. Note the residual as a named gap for the tech_lead.

A14. Existing tests keep their names and their assertions. Report the before and after top-level test counts for internal/application, internal/api, internal/store/firestore and internal/domain. contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json is not edited: confirm by measurement that cap-human-input-request's declared owner_surfaces entry /v1/requirements/{requirement_id} already resolves against contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml, so no declaration change is needed, and never weaken a declaration to fit the implementation.

A15. Quota. Both commands go through s.mutate so the conservative mutation reservation is taken before anything is staged. Measure quota.MutationUsage and state in the evidence that the extra document written by the ask stays inside it; if it does not, stop and escalate rather than raising a budget.

A16. Component checks. devbox run --pure -- make component-application, component-api, component-web, component-store-memory, component-store-firestore, component-contracts and component-docs are each green, and devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts is green. component-store-firestore runs under scripts/firestore-emulator.sh: actually run the emulator. A skipped test is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7); record every skip with status "skipped" and its reason, and never report a skipped suite as a passing one.

A17. Evidence. Create one artifact per touched component: .agents/v2/evidence/V2-065-{application,api,web,store-memory,store-firestore,contracts,docs}.json with ids ev-v2-065-{component}, all with task_id V2-065 and correlation_id v2-065-human-input-surface. Each records, for every check, the argv actually executed, the working directory, the timeout and a summary stating the measured result, plus the execution environment identifier (uname -srm, go version, devbox environment). Register them with exactly one appended entry each in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json whose evidence_hash is the sha256 of that artifact's final committed bytes; touch no other task's entry. Completion of this task means the ledger test is green with the entries in place: devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts.

A18. Evidence keys are read on the final tree. Each record's evidence_key is its own component key read with devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys on the final tree where make check is green, with every touched file already git-added; a new file not yet in the index is invisible to that key. If a later commit moves a component's tracked content, re-run the verification and record both the old and the new key rather than erasing the first observation.
A19. devbox run --pure -- make check is green, and it is re-run after the evidence commit so the secret scan reads committed history rather than an uncommitted tree. Record both runs.

A20. No file outside allowed_paths changes. ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum, devbox.*, internal/domain/**, internal/release/** and contracts/release-contract/** are untouched. If the work appears to require a new component or a new ci/components.json dependency edge, do not edit the file: stop and escalate with the exact edge you would have needed.
